review.verdict: The casting and style are solid (robot for AI, humans for people, consistent riso-duotone look), but the mechanics of the joke don't connect: the robot's hand never reaches the meter, the two panels bleed into each other with overlapping hands and a puzzle that crosses the divider, and the coins clip the canvas edge — this needs a composition pass before it's ready to publish.
revisionNotes: Robot's arms are up in a neutral/cheer pose, not touching the meter — the drain mechanic isn't shown. Give bot arms='reach' and move it to x≈0.25 so its hand visibly contacts the meter base.

The tired person's and shopper's hands overlap right at the divider, making the two 'panels' read as one merged scene with figures holding hands across the line. Pull shopper to x≈0.68 and keep its point gesture clear of the divider.
Coins clip the canvas edge (x912–1055 of 1080, per lint). Scale coins to 0.8 and move offset inward so they sit fully inside the safe area.
The puzzle crosses the divider into the right panel, breaking the two-panel split. Shift puzzle offset left so it stays fully in the left panel.

No gesture connects the shopper to the HUMAN MADE artwork — coins float near the top-right corner instead of being extended toward the frame. Move coins to the shopper's outstretched hand, aimed at the artwork.
This vertical-divider, human-vs-robot split layout is close to recent pieces ('Unnoticed', 'Records'); vary the panel framing (e.g. a counter/shelf split or diagonal horizon) next time.

review.verdict: The riso-duotone palette is consistent, but the brief's two-panel split was dropped in favor of one crowded row of 8 overlapping elements, the meter floats disconnected from the robot's drain gesture, and the robot is clipped at the left edge — the joke doesn't read in 3 seconds. revisionNotes: Rebuild as two actual panels with a divider, per the brief: left = bot + person + puzzle + meter, right = shopper + coins + artwork + label. Cap each panel at 2 main elements; right now 8 elements run together in one crowded row.

Connect the meter to the drain action: it floats isolated top-left with no line to the robot's hand and no tap gesture (arms are 'out', not reaching up). Move meter to attachTo person/top, and pose the robot arm reaching up to tap it.
Shift the robot right and/or scale it down (currently ~0.78) — lint confirms it's clipped at the left safe-area edge (x 2…405).
Separate the puzzle prop from the person's legs: the dark vertical bar currently fuses into the body creating an unreadable shape. Offset it further below/beside, not behind the legs.
Scale up the coins and move them into the shopper's hand — currently two tiny dots overlapping the artwork frame's corner, unreadable as 'coins' or as being handed over.
Reposition the HUMAN MADE label so it only sits under the artwork — it currently stretches across and overlaps both the shopper's and robot's legs.

review.verdict: The concept is on-brief (human person/shopper, robot only for AI) but the key visual links are missing: the meter floats unconnected above the robot, the puzzle is too small to read, and the coins have a rendering glitch — so the joke doesn't land within 3 seconds. Needs a revision pass before publishing.
revisionNotes: Give the robot a raised arm reaching to the meter so the drain action reads; right now the meter floats disconnected near the top of the canvas with no visual link to the robot below it.
Scale the puzzle prop up (from 0.7) and move it right under/overlapping the person's lap so the half-colored/half-outline split reads as a puzzle; at current size it reads as a stray color swatch.
Fix the coins raw shape: one circle renders as a faint translucent ghost overlapping another, looking like a rendering bug; render all three as solid accent-color circles with clear spacing.
Reposition the HUMAN MADE label directly beneath the artwork frame; it currently sits beside/overlapping the shopper's raised arm and reads as attached to the person instead of the art.
Both panels leave large empty bands in the vertical middle of the frame; pull the meter and artwork down and the puzzle/coins up so elements cluster into one balanced focal zone per panel.
Clarify the seated person's pose — the single vertical line under the torso reads as a cane or stray leg rather than a sitting posture; add a visible stool/seat shape or bent-leg silhouette.
